analysis:
The change in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop+EngineV2.swift is a refactor of KV-grant re-slicing. It adds a private static helper `minimumGrantBytes(_:)` and passes the per-slot serviceability floors as a new `minimumGrantBytes:` argument to `EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants` at four call sites: `reserveRaiseKeepsSurvivorsServiceable`, `resliceAndBuildEngineV2Bundle` (including the assistant fallback recompute), `resliceShrinkingForNewcomer` and `resliceGrowSurvivorsLocked`. The floors were already used for the post-hoc `resliceMeetsServiceabilityFloor` check. Now the same floors also shape the targets, so a slot funded to its floor is not shrunk back below it.

I saw no change to authentication, attestation, encryption, key handling, prefix-cache crypto, the SSD cache tier or any coordinator interface. The patch does not touch T-041's controls: HMAC lookup tags, TTL, salt scoping and the KEK purge. Prefix-cache-related KV budget carving is unchanged in kind.

Security relevance is limited to availability and resource accounting (T-029, T-016-style resource pressure). The floors are computed once from the `existing` snapshot, so the pre-shrink refusal still runs on the post-floor targets. The sum-of-grants ≤ budget invariant now depends on the unseen `EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants` implementation honoring the floors without exceeding the fleet budget. That implementation is outside the supplied evidence. If the floors can force the sum above the budget, over-subscription would be hidden. The unchanged `resliceMeetsServiceabilityFloor` check and the shared KV gate reject over-admission at runtime, so no concrete regression is evident. The next review pass should confirm that `resliceGrants` clamps the sum to the budget when floors exceed it.

The duplicate-key risk in `Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:)` is pre-existing, because model IDs are slot keys and so are unique.
